chunks: And whatever in it is from Muḥammad ibn Ḥassān, I have narrated it from my father, and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥusayn ibn Aḥmad ibn Idrīs—may Allah be pleased with them—from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥassān.

key_terms.أَبِي: My father; one of the author’s transmission authorities in this chain.
key_terms.أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ: A transmitter in the sanad/isnad through whom the report is conveyed.
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ: May Allah be pleased with them; an honorific supplication for the named transmitters.
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I transmitted it; a statement of direct narration by the compiler.
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَسَّانَ: The narrator to whom this transmission chain leads.

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain to Muḥammad ibn Ḥassān in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh?
ai.summary: This passage clarifies the sanad/isnad through which the author transmits reports from Muḥammad ibn Ḥassān. It serves as a technical note of hadith transmission, identifying the intermediaries linking the compiler to that narrator.
